history.speaker: narrator
history.text: For several minutes, you work on descriptions that avoid turning each person into a single exemplary trait. Leila was not merely organized. Ruth was not merely kind. Dev was not simply cheerful. The permitted source material supports particular actions, jokes, preferences, and skills. You keep those particulars rather than manufacturing six inspirational biographies.

history.speaker: nessa
history.text: Do we include the disagreements people remember?

history.speaker: tomas
history.text: If relevant, supported, and appropriate to the permission. We don't need to make them flawless. We also don't need to collect every old irritation to prove they're human.

history.speaker: ada
history.text: Enough complexity to prevent sainthood, not an inventory of gossip.

history.speaker: narrator
history.text: Nessa nods and closes a folder whose contents have not been cleared for public use. She has learned something by looking at the permission sheet first. So have you: care is not only adding information. Sometimes it is preserving a boundary while keeping the important public evidence available.
